title: Preflight Simulation Harness for Safe Config Reverts and Cost-aware Batching
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Build a preflight simulation harness that can run proposed config changes (routing, batching, cache TTLs, quantization flags) against representative traffic in a sandbox to produce deterministic regressions and cost delta estimates. The harness should: 1) replay a configurable set of real or synthetic requests in an isolated environment that mirrors production model variants and runtime kernels; 2) simulate KV cache warmup/eviction patterns and mark a quarantined cache state so we can detect cache-residency-sensitive regressions; 3) produce a compact rollback scoreboard (confidence, latency delta, token-cost delta, failure regression score) to feed the automatic rollback decision engine or a human review UI; 4) emit artifacts (replay traces, per-route latency histograms, token-level cost breakdown, diffed outputs for a golden prompt set) suitable for telemetry and post-mortem; 5) integrate with the apply pipeline to optionally block or auto-tag risky config changes for manual approval.

Background: We've seen config rollouts that interact unexpectedly with batching and KV caching heuristics — e.g., small changes to batch size or prefix-caching TTL producing tail latency regressions and token-cost spikes once the cache warmup profile diverges from the canary traffic. Existing automated rollback controllers rely on production signals that often arrive after user impact. A preflight simulation can reduce blast radius by surfacing regressions earlier and by providing a reversible, repeatable way to validate rollouts.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Harness can run a replay of a 24-hour sampled traffic window within a sandboxed cluster and finish a full simulation within 90 minutes for medium-sized customers.
- Detect and report cache-residency divergence with a metric: "stale_kv_delta" (percentage of responses hitting different KV state vs baseline).
- Provide cost delta estimate per 1M tokens and per-route, with 95% CI, and flag >10% adverse delta compared to baseline.
- Produce a rollback_score (0-100) combining reliability, performance, and economic signals that the AutoRollback service can consume. 
- Integration tests (CI) that validate harness against three synthetic scenarios: cold-cache startup, bursty latency spike, and steady-state throughput with quantization toggle.

Technical approach: 
- Replay engine: use sanitized request logs from the Request-Shadowing pipeline and the synthetic workload generator to produce deterministic sequences. Leverage a replay wrapper that deterministically scrubs non-deterministic metadata (timestamps, request IDs) and replays request timing distributions.
- Sandbox runtime: spin up a mirror runtime with identical model variant and kernel selectors but isolated storage and network. Use containerized GPU pools with configurable KV stores to emulate warm vs cold cache states.
- KV quarantine: before applying change, checkpoint current KV shards and create a shadow namespace. The harness will replay traffic into two namespaces (baseline vs proposed) and compute per-request KV residency differences.
- Cost estimation: instrument token emission and kernel selection paths to compute micro-cost metrics (GPU cycles estimate, kernel invocation counts) and combine with our billing model to produce per-token and per-route cost deltas.
- Rollback scoreboard: normalize signals (latency p95 delta, error-rate increase, stale_kv_delta, cost delta) into a single score and emit a rationale object (flat text) for each top contributor.
- Blocking/approval integration: if rollback_score exceeds an auto-fail threshold or cost delta > threshold, the pipeline either blocks the apply and opens a manual review ticket, or tags the rollout as "requires hold" in the Console.

Rollout plan: 
- Phase 1 (MVP, 3 sprints): implement replay engine + sandbox runtime + basic per-route latency/cost diff and artifacts.
- Phase 2 (2 sprints): KV quarantine and stale_kv_delta metric, rollout scoreboard, GitHub Action to run preflight on PRs that change runtime configs.
- Phase 3 (2 sprints): integrate with AutoRollback controller, add UI in Console for preflight report and one-click rollback.

Monitoring & playbook: 
- Dashboards: preflight success rate, time-to-simulate, distribution of rollback_score for proposals, false-positive rate vs historical reverts.
- Playbook: if preflight fails but apply was allowed (edge case), trigger a canary rollback with KV quarantine healing steps and open an incident with a standardized template.

Test plan: unit tests for scrubbers, end-to-end (CI) simulation that validates metric deltas against known golden results, and synthetic chaos tests that flip kernel selection mid-simulation to validate scoreboard sensitivity.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: simulation divergence from production due to infra differences. Mitigation: require the sandbox to use same kernel binary and model artifact; run nightly calibration against production small sample.
- Risk: long simulation times for large tenants. Mitigation: sample traffic using stratified reservoir sampling and provide a fast-preview mode focusing on cost-critical routes.
- Risk: false confidence from synthetic data. Mitigation: prefer sampled real requests for high-risk rollouts and mandate full preflight for P0 config changes.

Open questions: 
- Should the preflight harness be mandatory for any runtime-config change that touches batching, cache policies, or kernel selection? (Product decision)
- What is the canonical rollback_score threshold for auto-fail vs manual review? Proposed starting point: 65.
